speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've had this painful ulcer on your leg, and have you noticed any recent changes in its appearance or size?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and the location of this painful ulcer, I need to know if you currently experience any abdominal pain, diarrhea, or recent flare-ups of your bowel symptoms? Also, have you noticed any other skin lesions or joint pain elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of an ant bite followed by a necrotic ulcer with purplish borders, does the lesion have a distinct "crater-like" appearance with a raised, rolled edge, and have you developed any fever or chills since the bite? REQUEST TEST: Wound culture and PCR for Leishmania species.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin Biopsy Histopathology: Neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum. WBC: Normal. Blood Glucose (Random): Elevated. Temperature: 37.6°C (98°F).

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy confirming neutrophilic infiltration without infection strongly supports a diagnosis of Pyoderma Gangrenosum, likely associated with your Crohn's disease. To ensure we aren't missing a secondary issue given your diabetes, does the lesion show any signs of spreading rapidly or do you feel generally unwell? DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
